SaaS & startups / Consumer & mobile apps

Lifecycle messaging and store operations that respect users

For consumer and mobile apps with free tiers, subscriptions or in-app purchases. We build lifecycle push, email and WhatsApp journeys from product events, trial and renewal notices, store-aware payment recovery, review replies and user-content moderation, with frequency caps and clear opt-outs.

The challenge

What makes consumer & mobile apps different.

01

Lifecycle messages run on a calendar instead of on what the user did, so they read as nagging.

02

Subscription billing is split across App Store, Google Play and web checkout, each with its own renewal and retry rules.

03

Store reviews go unanswered, and bug reports hidden in one-star reviews never reach engineering.

04

Apps with user-generated content need filtering, reporting and blocking to meet App Store and Google Play rules.

05

Under India's DPDP Rules, users under 18 will need verifiable parental consent once the main duties apply in May 2027, which changes onboarding and analytics.

Where automation helps

Practical uses for consumer & mobile apps.

01

Behavior-based lifecycle journeys

Trigger push, email or WhatsApp messages from product events such as an unfinished first session or a lapsed habit, with frequency caps, quiet hours and per-channel opt-outs.

02

Transparent trial and renewal notices

Remind users before a trial converts or a plan renews, with the price, the date and a one-step route to cancel.

03

Store-aware payment recovery

Listen to App Store and Google Play subscription notifications and Stripe web billing events, and show the right in-app prompt for each case.

04

Review reply drafting

Draft replies to App Store and Google Play reviews in the reviewer's language for a person to approve, and turn bug reports into tickets.

05

User-content moderation

Filter and queue reported posts, profiles and messages for moderators, with blocking and appeal routes users can find.

Automation blueprints

The automations we would start with.

Open each blueprint for its trigger, steps, tools, human checkpoint, data handling, deliverables, and measures.

Sign up & activateStandard3–4 weeks

Event-driven onboarding and activation journeys

In-product tips, email, push and opt-in WhatsApp messages triggered by what each new user or workspace has and has not done, stopping the moment the activation milestone is reached.

B2B SaaS · Consumer & mobile apps

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Onboarding drips run on a fixed calendar, so users who already succeeded keep getting tips and users stuck on step two get nothing specific. Product teams cannot see which message helped and which only added noise.

Trigger

A signup event in PostHog followed by the absence of the next onboarding event within an agreed window, for example no data source connected within a day of creating a workspace, or no completed first session in a consumer app.

How it runs

  • Agree the activation milestone and the three to five steps before it, and map each step to a PostHog event and cohort.
  • Write one message per stuck step: an in-product checklist item, a Resend or Brevo email, a mobile push, or an approved WhatsApp template for users in India who opted in.
  • Check frequency caps, quiet hours and channel preferences before each send, and stop the journey as soon as the milestone event fires.
  • Keep a holdout group so the team can compare activation with and without the messages.
  • Report activation by cohort, step drop-off and opt-outs in a weekly view for the product lead.

Human checkpoint

The product or growth lead approves every message, cap and stop rule before launch and reviews the weekly cohort view. Changes to the activation definition need product and revenue sign-off.

Tools

Systems it connects

  • Product database
  • Firebase Cloud Messaging or OneSignal
  • In-app messaging (Intercom or custom)

Data & consent

Uses event names, timestamps and account identifiers, not the content users create or upload. Promotional messages respect consent and opt-outs; onboarding messages stay within service purposes. Accounts known to belong to users under 18 are excluded from behavior-based journeys, in line with the DPDP Act's limits on tracking children.

What we deliver

  • Activation milestone and event specification
  • Message matrix with caps and stop rules
  • Live journeys with a holdout group
  • Weekly activation cohort view

How we measure it

  • Activation rate within the agreed window
  • Step-level drop-off
  • Message opt-out rate
  • Time to first value

Convert & payStandard2–4 weeks

Trial-to-paid nudges with clear renewal notices

Trial reminders tailored to what each account actually used, stating the conversion date, the price including any GST and the cancellation route plainly, with high-fit trials flagged to sales.

B2B SaaS · Consumer & mobile apps

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Every trial user gets the same countdown emails. People who never reached value are pushed to pay, people who did are not reminded what they set up, and some trials convert without a clear notice, which India's dark patterns guidelines list as a SaaS billing dark pattern.

Trigger

Stripe's customer.subscription.trial_will_end event (sent three days before the trial ends), an App Store or Google Play trial status change, or a usage event showing the account hit a paid-plan limit.

How it runs

  • Join the trial's plan and dates from Stripe with PostHog usage to place the account in one of a few agreed states, such as activated, partly activated or inactive.
  • Send the reminder for that state, naming the conversion date, the amount including any GST and a one-step cancellation link, or the store's subscription settings for App Store and Google Play trials.
  • Offer inactive trials help or an extension instead of a payment push, and show activated ones a summary of what they set up.
  • Create a sales task for high-fit B2B trials so an account executive can offer a call before the trial ends.
  • Log every notice sent against the subscription so support can answer renewal questions.

Human checkpoint

The revenue lead approves pricing copy, extension rules and any discount beyond the agreed band. Your legal or compliance owner reviews any trial that collects a card or mandate upfront, since India's guidelines treat forcing payment details for a free subscription as a subscription trap.

Tools

SStripePPostHognn8nRResendHHubSpot

Systems it connects

  • Stripe Billing or Razorpay Subscriptions
  • App Store Connect
  • Google Play Console

Data & consent

Uses plan, trial dates, billing status and aggregate usage only; card details stay with the payment provider. Notices are service messages tied to the subscription, and the log of notices sent is kept for the life of the subscription plus the agreed record period.

What we deliver

  • Trial state definitions
  • Notice templates with price, date and cancellation link
  • Sales task rules for high-fit trials
  • Notice log linked to each subscription

How we measure it

  • Trial-to-paid conversion
  • Refund requests in the first billing period
  • Trial extensions granted and later converted
  • Cancellation reasons by trial state

Renew & retainStandard3–4 weeks

Failed-payment recovery and mandate-aware dunning

Payment failures are classified by cause and channel: India-issued card and UPI renewals get a link to authenticate or switch payment method, store subscriptions follow App Store and Google Play rules, and key accounts reach a person before any downgrade.

B2B SaaS · Consumer & mobile apps

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Renewals fail for expired cards, insufficient funds or missing authentication. Stripe attempts India-issued card renewals only once, App Store and Google Play run their own retries, and generic reminder emails do not tell customers what they actually need to do.

Trigger

Stripe invoice.payment_failed or invoice.payment_action_required events, a Razorpay subscription.pending or subscription.halted event, or App Store and Google Play notifications for billing retry, grace period or account hold.

How it runs

  • Classify the failure by provider, card origin, decline reason and whether authentication or a mandate is missing.
  • For India-issued cards and UPI Autopay, follow each provider's retry rules and send a hosted link to authenticate or switch payment method by email and, where the customer opted in, an approved WhatsApp utility template.
  • For international cards, let Stripe Smart Retries run and time reminders around the retry schedule.
  • For App Store and Google Play subscriptions, show an in-app prompt to update payment in the store and never ask for card details in the app.
  • Apply the agreed grace period through a feature flag on the account, then move it to the free plan rather than deleting data.
  • Alert the account owner and finance in Slack before a high-value B2B account is downgraded.

Human checkpoint

Finance owns the grace-period and downgrade policy. Customer success decides manual extensions or invoice payment for key accounts, and this workflow never deletes account data.

What we deliver

  • Recovery messages for each failure case
  • Grace-period and downgrade logic
  • Recovery dashboard by cause and provider

How we measure it

  • Involuntary churn
  • Time from failure to recovery
  • Key accounts downgraded without prior contact

Use, match & get helpAdvanced5–8 weeks

Trust and safety moderation queue

Listings, reviews, profiles and messages are screened with rules and a moderation model, risky items are held for trained moderators, and every decision, notice and appeal is recorded with a policy reason.

Marketplaces & platforms · Consumer & mobile apps

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Prohibited items, fake reviews, harassment and off-platform contact details reach users before anyone checks. User reports pile up in an inbox, decisions vary by moderator, and the team cannot show how fast complaints were handled.

Trigger

New or edited user content, a user report, or a complaint sent to the grievance officer.

How it runs

  • Run rule checks such as banned-item terms, phone numbers in listings and price outliers, then a moderation model on text and images.
  • Publish low-risk items, hold medium-risk items for review, and block high-risk items until a moderator decides.
  • Show each item in a Retool queue with the policy clause, user history and prior reports, sorted by severity and deadline.
  • Record the moderator's decision with a reason code, notify the user and offer an appeal route.
  • Track complaints against the IT Rules timelines: acknowledgment within 24 hours and resolution within seven days, with faster handling for the categories the Rules specify.
  • Review overturned decisions monthly to tune rules and model thresholds.

Human checkpoint

Trained moderators decide removals and warnings; suspensions and bans need a senior reviewer. Law enforcement requests and legal notices go to the grievance officer and counsel, never to automation.

Tools

OOpenAIRRetoolSSupabasenn8nSSlack

Systems it connects

  • Help desk with grievance queue
  • In-app report and block features

Data & consent

Moderators see user content and reporter identity, so access is role-based and logged, and reporters are never revealed to the reported user. Graphic images are blurred by default in the queue. Decision logs are kept for the period the client's counsel sets for legal defense and regulatory requests.

What we deliver

  • Content policy mapped to reason codes
  • Screening rules and model thresholds
  • Retool moderation and appeal queue
  • Grievance timeline tracker
  • Monthly moderation quality review

How we measure it

  • Report-to-action time
  • Grievances resolved within deadline
  • Appeal overturn rate
  • Harmful items found after publishing

Renew & retainStarter2–3 weeks

App store review response drafting

New App Store and Google Play reviews are collected, classified and answered with drafts that follow each store's reply policies and are approved by a person, with bug and billing reports turned into tickets.

Consumer & mobile apps

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Reviews arrive in two consoles and several languages. Unanswered complaints weaken the store listing, and real bug reports hidden in one-star reviews never reach engineering.

Trigger

A new or edited review fetched at least daily through the App Store Connect API and the Google Play Developer API; the Play API returns only reviews from the past week, so the schedule must not lapse.

How it runs

  • Fetch new reviews with app version, country, language and rating.
  • Classify each review as bug, billing, feature request, praise or abusive, and note the app version involved.
  • Draft a reply in the reviewer's language that addresses their point, contains no personal information and does not promote anything.
  • Create a Jira issue for reproducible bugs and a support case for billing problems, linked to the review.
  • Post the reply through the store API after a person approves or edits it, and send weekly themes to the product team.

Human checkpoint

The community or support lead approves or edits every reply before it is posted. Refunds for store purchases follow App Store and Google Play processes and are never promised in a reply.

Tools

  • Google Play Console

Data & consent

  • Approval queue for drafted replies

Learn, ship & reportStandard3–5 weeks

Feedback-to-roadmap loop with release notes

Survey answers, reviews, tickets and sales notes are tagged into one feedback base linked to Jira, and when a fix or feature ships, release notes are drafted and sent to the users who asked for it.

B2B SaaS · Consumer & mobile apps · AI-first products

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Feedback is scattered across surveys, support tickets, store reviews and call notes. Product managers prioritize from memory, and users who asked for a change rarely hear that it shipped.

Trigger

A new PostHog survey response, tagged ticket, store review or sales note; separately, a GitHub release or Jira fix version marked as released.

How it runs

  • Collect feedback into one Airtable base with source, user segment and plan.
  • Tag theme, product area and sentiment with an AI model and suggest links to existing Jira issues for a product manager to confirm.
  • Send detractor responses from paying users to the account or support owner as a follow-up task.
  • On release, gather merged changes and linked issues and draft a changelog entry and in-app note in plain language.
  • After approval, publish the notes and email only the users who requested the change or use the affected feature.
  • Post a weekly theme digest to the product channel in Slack.

Human checkpoint

Product managers decide priorities and confirm every suggested merge. The product owner approves release notes, and the engineering lead reviews notes on security fixes and breaking changes before publication.

Tools

Systems it connects

  • App Store Connect and Google Play Console
  • Changelog page

Data & consent

Feedback is stored with user identifiers so requesters can be told when a change ships; free-text answers are not used for advertising. Release emails go only to users whose preferences allow product updates, and feedback records are kept for the agreed period.

What we deliver

  • Unified feedback base with tagging
  • Jira linking with merge review
  • Release note drafting and targeted send
  • Weekly feedback theme digest

How we measure it

  • Detractor follow-up time
  • Time from release to announcement
  • Adoption of released features among requesters
